problem_statement:
Bug#33064461 - WRONGLY HANDLED DEFINER FOR TRIGGERS WHEN PS USED

When prepared statement(PS) is used, INVOKER privileges are used
to check table access instead of DEFINER privileges for triggers
created with the DEFINER clause. Hence, privilege checks to tables
used in triggers failed. This issue exists even with the stored
functions.

While opening tables for the statement execution, even tables used
by triggers and stored functions are opened and added as a not own
tables to the query table list. In PS module, before executing
statement, privilege check for all the tables is done. At this
stage, we incorrectly check access for tables used by trigger/stored
function. Privilege check for such tables is done in the Stored
Program(SP) module using the privileges of DEFINER or INVOKER.

To fix this issue, changed code to check access for only own
tables before executing statement in the PS module. Access for
tables used by trigger / stored function is checked in the SP
module.
